correctness.rationale: In a crown of n≥3 the deleted partners are distance 3, and a third vertex has distances 1 and 2 from them. Thus no third vertex can strongly resolve that pair and every strong resolving set meets it. Conversely, for two omitted vertices from different pairs, the selected partner of one is a resolving witness: the other omitted vertex lies on a length-three geodesic between partners. Pairs meeting S are resolved by their selected endpoint. Among sets with pair coverage, an omitted a_i is undominated precisely when no b_j with j≠i is selected; pair coverage then forces b_i and all a_j with j≠i into S. This leaves exactly the stated two families, distinct for n≥3. Each matched index has factor 2z+z², and deleting the 2n size-n exceptions gives the polynomial and coefficient 2^n−2n>0 at z^n. Independent BFS-distance and closed-neighborhood tests cover all 87,360 subsets for n=3 through 8, finding 9,762 qualifying sets and 438 total minimum sets.
residual_risks: The BFS replay is exhaustive only in the stated range. The arbitrary-n claim follows from the exact metric and domination arguments; n=2 is disconnected and excluded.

evidence: The direct-product strong-metric theorem gives the matched-pair cover precursor. The strong-resolving-domination papers inspected treat joins/coronas and lexicographic products; the diameter-at-most-two scalar corollary is inapplicable at diameter three.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Strong metric dimension alone is a lower bound and a whole shore attains it while dominating. Neither this scalar argument nor the two domination papers alone give the exceptional pattern census; the indexed disjoint branch does.

originality.rationale: The known strong resolving graph nK_2 makes strong resolution equivalent to disjoint sets of omitted indices on the two shores. A distinct same-day Resultary solid-locating-domination result already states and counts exactly the dominating disjoint-omission branch, with the same exceptions and size polynomial. Its extra n matched-pair omissions are precisely the branch excluded by strong resolution. The entire frozen result, not just its scalar, follows by selecting the existing branch. This is demonstrable coverage, not a claim about ordering or historical priority.
residual_risks: The 2025 dominant strong metric dimension text remains uninspected; the public search was uninformative. The failure rests on positive catalogue and direct-product coverage, not absence or inaccessibility. Same-day labels do not establish priority.
